answer: Treat identity as an uncacheable route: pin each agent to a graph vertex. Each epoch a public beacon draws a wander path; the agent must return in one round trip a chained proof bearing every hop's lantern, a value only that node holds and publishes after the deadline. Paths are set at query time and lanterns do not yet exist, so one machine cannot precompute replies for a thousand aliases: each fake needs its own live graph slice. Co-hosted aliases leak matching latency, so clustering slashes the whole bond. Attackers pay in separated, always-on nodes per identity; honest agents pay once.
